statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is 16% and remains below the watch threshold, while Stress is held elevated at 58% because the opening bounce was fully surrendered against a 4.73% 10-year, a 5.27% 30-year and a $94 Brent risk premium.
recommendation: The mapped policy state remains EA_ON. One narrow window is flagged, 19:00Z to 20:00Z, covering the power hour on August monthly options expiry, where closing and roll flow concentrate while the long end sits at session highs. The elevated Stress reading describes cross-asset conflict rather than observed one-way Nasdaq-100 structure: the cash index has traded both sides of its opening range and retracements remain present in the observed price path. From 21:00Z US index futures are scheduled to halt for the weekend, so the remainder of the horizon carries a closed-market baseline.
headline: The Nasdaq-100 has given back its entire gap-up open after a hot flash services PMI lifted yields, but the fade is two-sided rather than one-way.
body: Cash NDX trades near 29,245, about +0.11% against a 29,213.17 prior close, after covering both sides of a 29,179.23-29,366.12 range in the first forty minutes of the session; NQ September futures sit near 29,272, about -0.09%, against a 29,539.00 overnight high and a 29,300.50 prior close. The opening gain built on an attempt to snap a five-day Nasdaq-100 slump has therefore been fully surrendered, but the index has already retraced off its session low, so the observed structure is a two-sided whipsaw rather than persistent directional extension. The proximate driver is the 13:45Z S&P Global flash PMI pair: services printed 56.8 against 54.0 expected and 54.6 prior, the strongest since December 2024, lifting the composite to 56.0 and the fastest output growth in over four years, while manufacturing slipped to a five-month low of 53.2 on Strait of Hormuz supply disruption. That mix reduces near-term easing odds and pushed the 2-year up about 3 basis points to 4.23%, the 10-year to 4.73% and the 30-year to 5.27%. Against that, VIX is 15.42 and down about 3.7%, which argues against a panic regime, while breadth is rotational rather than uniform: the Dow is outperforming, semiconductors were the weakest tracked group in the latest session and megacap performance was mixed. Brent near $93.66 and WTI near $86.42 are marginally lower on the day but on track for a second consecutive weekly gain of roughly 5%, with Treasury measures to isolate Iran's economy scheduled to be detailed on Monday. Tail is therefore held low at 16% and Stress elevated at 58%. The remaining intraday concentration point is the 19:00Z power hour on August monthly options expiry, after which US index futures halt for the weekend from 21:00Z. The week ahead brings Case-Shiller and consumer confidence on August 25, then the GDP second estimate, July PCE and durable goods on August 26.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: seven hourly assessments are available (01:00Z, 06:00Z, 07:00Z, 08:00Z, 11:00Z, 12:00Z and 13:00Z) and the remaining seventeen clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available slots Tail stayed tightly contained between 12% and 15% with a green mapped state throughout, Stress decayed from 59% to 53% through the quiet overnight and European morning before rebuilding to 57% as the US open and the flash PMI pair approached, and Confidence improved from 83% to a 86-87% plateau as more of the session's evidence became verifiable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds the current hour and the next at the post-event level while the flash PMI repricing settles and the European cash close passes, then decays toward the session baseline through the New York afternoon on the assumption that price discovery stays orderly and retracements keep appearing. One watch-level hour is carried at 19:00Z, where August monthly options expiry concentrates closing and roll flow against session-high long-end yields; expiry swings are typically two-sided and pin-driven, so the step up is deliberately narrow. From 21:00Z US index futures are scheduled to halt for the weekend, so the final seventeen slots carry a closed-market floor: Tail falls to 6-8% because no tradable price path exists, Stress sits in the moderate band reflecting weekend headline exposure through the Iran and oil channel ahead of Monday's Treasury announcement, and Confidence decays from 72% to 63% purely as a function of distance from the last verified market observation.
